items.title: Laurence Juber interviewed by Monk Rowe, Glasgow, Scotland, July 27, 2016 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: And he became my kind of studio mentor.

ctx.x: I borrowed some Wings LPs from my brother. And it turned out that what we played was some Chuck Berry tunes and some reggae grooves and they offered me the gig. But when I got to L.A. it was a very different world, because the union, the AF of M was much more involved than the English musicians’ union. So all of a sudden I find myself — you know I did some jingle sessions in New York for Lincoln Mercury and then all of a sudden I’m getting all these checks. Whereas in England I’d go to an 8 AM jingle and you’d…

He’d seen me on television with the National Youth Jazz Orchestra and called me up the next day and said — he called everybody darling. He said, “Darling, I’ve got some sessions for you.” And he gave me the dates. I said, “David, I hate to say this, but those are my final exams for my bachelor of music degree.” And I just couldn’t — you know I’d been studying for three years, I wasn’t going to skip the finals. And I didn’t think I’d hear from him again, but as it turned out he called a couple of weeks later. And…
Well this may be a silly questions, but did your ears and hearing survive the Wings experience?
